name: Interactive Linear Algebra (Dan Margalit and Joseph Rabinoff)
goodFor: An introductory linear algebra textbook with interactive figures and exercises, written for Georgia Tech's Math 1553.
attribution: "Dan Margalit and Joseph Rabinoff, Interactive Linear Algebra", linked to https://textbooks.math.gatech.edu/ila/, with the section named; "GNU Free Documentation License", linked to https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html; and, when the text shown was shortened or changed, a note that it was.

notes: Checked against the book's Colophon and Preface: copyright 2017 Georgia Institute of Technology, licensed under GFDL 1.2 or any later version with no Invariant Sections and no Cover Texts, which allows commercial use; the book includes the licence's text as an appendix. The Preface says Rabinoff made all the figures and demos and that all source code may be freely copied under the same licence; Larry Rolen wrote many of the exercises. The demos run on the third-party MathBox framework, whose licence wasn't read. The site has no separate terms-of-use page; none was found. GFDL requires a distributed copy or extract to keep the copyright and licence notices and be accompanied by the licence text (or a link an app shows with it), and a modified version stays under the GFDL. The title page gives 2019. A LibreTexts adaptation exists and was not read. The bank's agents don't read it and nothing from it goes into the bank.
